description: Apply one operation to one or more images, or render a template: edit, remove_bg, upscale, restore_face, colorize, analyze, resize, convert, compress, crop, pad, grayscale, rotate, flip, flop, trim, flatten, adjust, mask, blur_region, overlay, caption, render_template, read_metadata (built-in list — GET /api/v1/ops could not be read, so an op added since this release may be missing). Inputs are asset ids, local file paths (stdio) or public URLs. ONE local file or URL with a deterministic op runs synchronously and NOTHING is stored in the account (no asset id): the result is written to a temp file on this machine and the answer carries its `path`. Several images, asset ids, or any AI op run as a job and return asset ids and public URLs. Neither mode ever returns image bytes. render_template takes no images: parameters {templateId (id or id@version), items: [one object of template variables per PNG]}. variants gives several outputs from one call as ONE job (e.g. every social size). read_metadata costs no credits; a local file stores nothing, but urls are ingested first, so each becomes an asset in the account and counts toward its asset quota. Cost: AI ops charge credits per item (see the estimate); deterministic ops (resize/convert/compress/crop/pad/grayscale/rotate/flip/flop/trim/flatten/adjust/mask/blur_region/overlay/caption/render_template) are free on paid plans and count against the Free plan's monthly quota. Set dry_run=true to get the exact price without spending. Errors come back structured: `retryable` says whether the same call can be retried; `param` names the input to fix.

asset_ids.description: Existing asset ids to process — at most 500 in one call here; a bigger batch is the CLI's or an SDK's.

collection.description: Collection to put the new assets in (an opaque name; search_assets filters on it). Without one, an output made from an asset is in that asset's collection.

dry_run.description: Price only — nothing is created, uploaded or charged. asset_ids are priced as themselves; file_paths and urls by how many there are, since the price depends on the op, model and parameters, never on the image.

file_paths.description: Local files to upload first (only when the server runs on your machine over stdio).

idempotency_key.description: Your key for this submission. Calling again with the same key and the same arguments returns the job the first call created instead of submitting (and charging for) a second one; the same key with different arguments is refused with idempotency_key_reuse. Use one when you might retry after a timeout.

model.description: Override the op's default model (AI ops). Models with their prices: the resource imagestep://models/ai_image (imagestep://models/analyze for analyze).

parameters.description: Op parameters — resize {width,height,fit}; convert {format,quality}; crop {left,top,width,height}; pad {top,bottom,left,right,background}; upscale {scaleFactor} … (built-in summary: GET /api/v1/ops could not be read; the resource imagestep://ops/{op} has the contract when it can be).

publish.description: Publish result assets so each output has a stable publicUrl on the CDN — the output itself at full size, not a thumbnail.

retention_days.description: Keep what this call stores — the images you hand it and the ones it makes — this many days instead of the account's plan retention. Shorter only: more is kept for the plan's time. Use it when the outputs are consumed at once (posted, sent on) and need not be kept.

urls.description: Public http(s) image URLs to ingest first.

variants.description: Several outputs from one call (contract §8): the op runs once per variant for every input image, in ONE job, and each variant is a new asset. Top-level `parameters` are the shared half, e.g. parameters {fit:"cover"} with variants [{"name":"ig","parameters":{"width":1080,"height":1350}},{"name":"x","parameters":{"width":1600,"height":900}}].

name.description: Unique within the call; each result item carries it as `variant`.

parameters.description: This variant's parameters, merged over the shared top-level `parameters`.

wait.description: Wait for the job to finish (up to wait_seconds) and return its outputs. false → return the job handle now; poll with job_status.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait when wait=true.

name: transform

analyses.description: An analyze job: one per completed item, the answer in output.

assets.description: read_metadata on assets: each one's id, name, image, metadata and expiresAt.

creditsCharged.description: What the job cost; a failed item is not charged.

error.description: A refused call (isError): code, message, retryable — whether the same call can succeed — and param, the input to fix.

errorCode.description: A failed job: the verdict on its failed items, from the closed set of error codes.

estimate.description: A dry run's answer: the price of exactly this call. Nothing was created or charged.

sufficientCredit.description: false: a real submit would answer insufficient_credit — stop and tell the person.

expiresAt.description: When the job record is swept: its retention, the same as the assets it made.

failedItems.description: Items that failed; with errorCode and retryable, the verdict on them.

image.description: read_metadata on a local file: what the image is.

items.description: One per input (per variant): its status, the ids in and out, the error, who ran it, how long and at what cost.

itemsNote.description: Only the first page of items is here: the job_status call (items_cursor) that reads on.

metadata.description: read_metadata on a local file: the file's metadata.

mode.description: Ran synchronously: nothing was stored and no asset id exists.

note.description: What to do next, in words.

op.description: The op it ran, when it ran one.

outputs.description: The assets a finished job made, with publicUrl when published — the first 20.

error.description: Why ingest failed, on a FAILED asset; retryable says whether uploading the file again can help.

expiresAt.description: When the asset is deleted (ISO 8601), if it has a retention.

outputsNote.description: The search_assets call (job_id and cursor) that reads the rest of the outputs.

outputsTruncated.description: More outputs than the answer carries.

path.description: Over stdio: the file, in this server's temp directory.

presetId.description: The preset it ran, when it ran one.

presetVersion.description: The preset version that ran: slug@version runs exactly it again.

retryable.description: A failed job: whether resuming it can succeed.

status.description: COMPLETED, FAILED or CANCELLED once it has stopped; anything else means it is still moving — poll job_status.

timedOut.description: The wait ran out, not the job: poll job_status with the jobId, never submit again.

totalItems.description: How many items: one per input (per variant).

type.description: The engine that ran it: ai-generate, ai-edit, parse, process, render, chain.

url.description: On the hosted server: a signed link to the bytes, valid for expiresInSeconds.

title: Run one atomic op on assets, or render a template
